2026-0.test: Right if, by the end of August 2026, frontier agents routinely complete computer tasks that take people several hours (with human review), and a lab reports research agents running for days or weeks under monitoring, with trajectory-level safeguards such as chain-of-thought or action monitoring adopted. Partly if only one half holds.

2026-1.test: Right if, by the end of November 2026, a leading lab discloses (or credible reporting shows) that roughly half of its compute goes to AI research and development, and labs or regulators name internal deployment as the main safety bottleneck. Partly if internal deployment becomes a major safety focus but the compute split isn't shown.

2026-2.test: Right if, by the end of May 2026, at least one frontier AI lab is valued at or near $1 trillion, AI infrastructure firms are worth trillions, and the industry shows exceptional political leverage (record lobbying, heavy election spending or direct deals with heads of government). Partly if only the valuations or only the leverage arrive.

2026-3.test: Right if, by the end of December 2026, credible reporting or company disclosures show at least a few thousand humanoid robots working on live production lines (not pilots or demos) across one or more manufacturers, while humanoids still do only narrow tasks. Partly if deployments reach the hundreds or stay in pilots.

2026-4.test: Right if, by the end of October 2026, both the US and the EU make pre-release review of the most capable models against cyber, bio and autonomy risks a standard step, by law, regulation or a binding government process covering the leading labs. Partly if it is standard in only one of them, or only voluntary.

2026-5.test: Right if, by the end of December 2026, at least one major government (such as the US, UK or EU) funds or runs a programme that tracks frontier AI compute or tests inference-only verification as part of its AI preparedness work. Partly if it stays at studies, consultations or pilot grants.

2026-6.test: Right if, by 31 December 2026, a released AI system matches skilled people across essentially all cognitive work, as judged by independent evaluations and broad expert agreement rather than a lab's own claim. A model marketed as AGI that experts dispute doesn't count.

2026-7.test: Right if, by the end of July 2026, a peer-reviewed paper reports one participant using an intracortical BCI at home for more than 3,800 hours of speech and cursor control, and Neuralink's PRIME-family studies are still early-feasibility safety trials, with no pivotal trial or approval. Partly if only one half holds.

2026-8.test: Right if, through 31 December 2026, launched GPUs run named AI workloads in orbit but no operator discloses utility-scale power and cooling for orbital compute (for example, megawatt-class power). Wrong if such a disclosure arrives within 2026.

2027-0.test: Right if, by the end of September 2027, company disclosures or credible estimates show AI agents earning at least $10 billion a month in paid work (about $120 billion a year) with millions of agent instances running continuously. Partly if revenue is in the billions a month but short of $10 billion.

2027-1.test: Right if, by the end of December 2027, credible surveys or repository data show that more than half of new production code is written end to end by AI, with people setting goals and reviewing exceptions. Partly if that holds only at leading tech firms, or only with line-by-line human editing.

2027-2.test: Right if, by the end of September 2027, frontier labs report that coding agents materially speed up their model research (a measured speed-up, or a large share of research code), while people still direct the research. Wrong if AI R&D is fully automated by then, or if no material speed-up is reported.

2027-3.test: Right if, by the end of December 2027, credible surveys or reporting show companies in every major industry (such as finance, health, manufacturing, retail, government and media) redesigning business models and workforces around AI at the same time. Partly if the disruption is clear in some industries but not all.

2027-4.test: Right if, by the end of December 2027, a federal US bill on AI transparency, compute tracking or frontier accountability passes at least one chamber of Congress or becomes law. Partly if it only clears a committee. State laws and executive orders don't count.

2027-5.test: Right if, by the end of October 2027, datacentre power, water or grid limits are a top-tier national political issue in the US or another major economy: national legislation, a head of government's priority, or projects blocked or delayed at scale. Partly if the fights stay local or state-level.

2028-0.test: Right if, by the end of March 2029, polls or exit polls in a major national election (such as the 2028 US presidential election) show AI, including its effect on jobs, as the single most important issue for voters. Partly if AI ranks among the top three issues.

2028-1.test: Right if, by the end of January 2029, labour-market data or large surveys show that in most white-collar occupations in a leading economy, the main work is directing, reviewing and coordinating AI agents. Partly if that's true only in some professions, such as software, finance or law.

2028-2.test: Right if, by the end of September 2028, frontier labs run large, ongoing programmes that train models profession by profession using paid experts, simulated work environments and data from real deployments, across many professions. Partly if it's limited to a few fields.

2028-3.test: Right if, by the end of February 2029, the frontier is held by no more than a handful of US and Chinese labs, and access, deployment and policy run through direct arrangements with the US president and China's party leadership. Partly if only the US half, or only the company concentration, holds.

2028-4.test: Right if, by the end of June 2028, announced or reported datacentre construction commitments for a single year exceed that year's US defence budget (about $850 billion or more), as tallied by credible analysts or official data. Partly if they exceed half of it.

2028-5.test: Right if, by the end of January 2029, an AI system clearly exceeds the best people across essentially all cognitive work and is substantially improving its own successors, as confirmed by independent evaluators rather than a lab's claim alone.

2028-6.test: Right if, by the end of March 2029, governments of the leading AI powers, including the US and China, open formal negotiations on slowing frontier AI development or auditing frontier compute. Partly if talks are informal, leave out the US or China, or stop at declarations.

2028-7.test: Right if, by the end of October 2028, a peer-reviewed paper publishes a synapse-resolution connectome of a whole vertebrate larval brain (such as a zebrafish larva), without a working emulation of that brain. Wrong if no such connectome is published by then.

2029-0.test: Right if, by the end of February 2030, official statistics or credible economic estimates show AI doing at least 25% of cognitive labour (by hours or value) in a leading economy. Partly if estimates land between 15% and 25%.

2029-1.test: Right if, by the end of November 2029, the US and China hold formal government-to-government negotiations covering declarations of frontier compute, inspections or limits on training runs. Partly if they only agree to talk, or discuss AI risk without compute or limits on the table.

2029-2.test: Right if, by the end of February 2030, the US and China both pause their largest frontier training runs under an agreement or matching commitments, while existing models keep running. Wrong if no such pause happens.

2029-3.test: Right if, by the end of March 2030, verification that a datacentre is only running inference (not training) is in use at two or more major datacentres, confirmed by a government, an auditor or the operators. Partly if it's at one site or only in trials.

2029-4.test: Right if, by the end of April 2030, a multilateral consortium or treaty framework on frontier AI is signed or joined by several major powers beyond the US and China. Partly if it stays at declarations or summit statements without a framework.

2029-5.test: Right if, by the end of October 2029, a government or a major party in a leading economy adopts AI dividends, sovereign stakes in AI firms or taxes on compute rents as policy, citing lost labour-tax revenue. Partly if it stays with think tanks and minor parties.

2029-6.test: Right if, by the end of August 2029, AI policy decisions (such as export controls, regulation or responses to AI job losses) trigger repeated major market swings over months, and polling shows AI policy splitting voters along party lines. Partly if only one of the two shows up.

2030-0.test: Right if, by the end of December 2030, AI systems do a frontier lab's AI research end to end (ideas, experiments, engineering and evaluation), with people only overseeing, as shown by the lab and independent evaluators. Partly if AI does most of it but people still run key steps.

2030-1.test: Right if, by the end of June 2031, AI that matches or beats top human experts across essentially all cognitive fields arrives within about a year of AI fully automating coding, as shown by independent evaluations. Wrong if coding is automated but top-expert AI is still more than about 18 months away.

2030-2.test: Right if, by the end of December 2030, after an agreed pause, frontier AI research restarts under rules that make the labs' research fully transparent to regulators and verified across borders. Wrong if no pause and restart under such rules happens.

2030-3.test: Right if, by the end of March 2031, frontier labs' algorithms and training methods are open to broad independent audit under law or treaty, while frontier model weights stay locked down against misuse. Partly if audits are voluntary or limited to one country.

2030-4.test: Right if, by the end of December 2030, the FDA, the EMA or another major regulator approves a drug whose molecule was substantially designed by AI, as stated by its developer and reported by credible outlets. Partly if approvals cover only drugs where AI helped with discovery but didn't design the molecule.

2030-5.test: Right if, by the end of March 2031, leading economists, central banks or the major AI firms name energy, chips, factories or robots, rather than research ideas or talent, as the main limit on AI-driven growth, with evidence such as long equipment or power backlogs. Partly if it's argued but disputed.

2031-0.test: Right if, by the end of January 2032, labs or independent evaluators show AI-run research making frontier AI progress about ten times faster than human-led research did. Partly if a measured speed-up of about three to ten times is shown.

2031-1.test: Right if, by the end of April 2032, official data or credible estimates for a leading economy show AI doing about a third of cognitive labour and robots about a tenth of physical labour. Partly if only one of the two levels is reached.

2031-2.test: Right if, by the end of September 2031, the combined annual revenue of the largest AI companies (the leading labs and AI infrastructure firms, as reported) is comparable to the annual revenue of a major national government such as Germany's, Japan's or the UK's. Partly if it reaches about half of it.

2031-3.test: Right if, by the end of March 2032, law or binding regulation in the US, the EU or another major jurisdiction requires published, externally reviewed safety cases before the highest-risk frontier models are deployed. Partly if safety cases are required but kept private, or stay voluntary.

2031-4.test: Right if, by the end of March 2032, after repeated agent incidents, law or binding regulation in a major jurisdiction requires trajectory-level monitoring and externally reviewed control cases for the highest-risk agent deployments. Partly if only labs' own policies or voluntary accords require them.

2031-5.test: Right if, by the end of May 2032, regulators or legislators in a major jurisdiction treat AI that keeps learning after deployment as a distinct problem (hearings, rules or enforcement) because its capabilities can change after approval. Partly if it's only raised in consultations.

2032-0.test: Right if, by the end of May 2033, official data or credible estimates show AI doing more than half of all cognitive labour (by hours or value) in at least one leading economy. Partly if the estimate is between 35% and 50%.

2032-1.test: Right if, by the end of May 2033, credible studies show commercially available robots able to perform about a third of economically valuable physical tasks (by share of tasks or value) at an acceptable cost. Partly if they can do about a fifth.

2032-2.test: Right if, by the end of August 2033, a leading economy's official statistics show real GDP growth of about 50% in a year, driven by AI. Partly if growth runs above 10% a year and is clearly AI-driven.

2032-3.test: Right if, by the end of October 2032, investment data show a surge of capital into mining, motors, actuators, chip fabs and factories, with robot hardware widely reported as the binding limit on AI-driven growth. Partly if the surge is confined to chips and power.

2032-4.test: Right if, by the end of March 2033, the US, the EU, China or another major jurisdiction caps, or auctions permits for, frontier compute or large-scale robot production. Partly if it only licenses or registers them without a cap.

2032-5.test: Right if, by the end of December 2032, at least one leading economy enacts taxes on compute, robots or automated capital that raise a material share of revenue (at least a few percent of tax receipts) or replace part of income tax. Partly if such taxes are enacted but raise little.

2033-0.test: Right if, by the end of June 2034, official statistics or credible estimates show AI and robots contributing at least half of economic output in a leading economy. Partly if the share is between a third and a half.

2033-1.test: Right if, by the end of January 2034, a major economy starts paying every citizen (or every adult) a recurring dividend funded by AI, compute or robot revenue. Partly if it's a one-off payment, a pilot, or limited to some groups.

2033-2.test: Right if, by the end of July 2034, governments formally negotiate how AI-generated wealth is shared across borders, at the UN, the G20 or in a treaty process. Partly if it stays in statements and proposals.

2033-3.test: Right if, by the end of May 2034, a major jurisdiction enacts limits on AI persuasion capabilities, binding disclosure rules for AI-targeted influence, or taxes on it, citing cheap AI persuasion. Partly if only voluntary platform policies exist.

2033-4.test: Right if, by the end of March 2034, usage data show personal AI advisors overtaking traditional search and social feeds as people's main way to find information in at least one leading economy. Partly if they're widely used but still second.

2033-5.test: Right if, by the end of September 2034, a lightly regulated AI-and-robot economy or industrial zone shows output or capacity doubling in under a year, in credible data. Partly if doubling takes one to two years.

2033-6.test: Right if, by the end of July 2034, major governments fund biodefence at population scale: continuous pathogen monitoring plus the capacity to make vaccines against a new threat within months. Partly if such programmes are funded but cover only part of it.

2034-0.test: Right if, by the end of July 2035, chipmakers or credible industry studies report that AI does most of the cognitive work in chip R&D and production engineering. Partly if AI does a large but minority share.

2034-1.test: Right if, by the end of April 2035, credible estimates or company disclosures show at least 100 million AI agent instances working continuously. Partly if it's at least 10 million.

2034-2.test: Right if, by the end of October 2035, credible estimates put global AI compute at several terawatts of power and billions of H100-equivalent chips. Partly if it reaches about a terawatt or hundreds of millions of H100-equivalents.

2034-3.test: Right if, by the end of September 2035, major powers adopt binding caps on frontier compute, or agreed provisions to disable each other's frontier compute if the rules are broken. Wrong if neither is adopted.

2034-4.test: Right if, by the end of May 2035, several large AI datacentres are built in neutral jurisdictions, at sea, or in other places chosen so they can be audited internationally. Partly if there's only one, or they're only announced.

2034-5.test: Right if, by the end of September 2035, a treaty signed by the major military powers limits the use of frontier AI in military R&D or in autonomous strategic weapons. Partly if there are only political declarations, or treaties without the US, China or Russia.

2035-0.test: Right if, by the end of May 2036, independent evaluations show the strongest AIs performing at the level of top human experts in essentially every cognitive field. Partly if they reach that level in most fields but not all.

2035-1.test: Right if, by the end of August 2036, the leading labs or governments hold frontier capability growth near top-expert level, explicitly because control methods no longer scale safely. Wrong if no such pause is in force.

2035-2.test: Right if, by the end of August 2036, official data or credible estimates show AI and robots doing at least 85% of economically valuable labour in a leading economy. Partly if the share is between 60% and 85%.

2035-3.test: Right if, by the end of March 2036, two or more major economies have a permanent, legislated universal high income or AI dividend paid to all citizens. Partly if it's in one economy, or temporary.

2035-4.test: Right if, by the end of July 2036, controlled studies show AI out-persuading the best human persuaders, and an international agreement strictly controls AI persuasion. Partly if only one half holds.

2035-5.test: Right if, by the end of September 2036, a major jurisdiction legislates on AI welfare or legal status, or major companies adopt formal AI welfare or compensation policies as standard governance. Partly if it stays at research programmes and voluntary statements.

2035-6.test: Right if, by the end of May 2036, labs or regulators routinely use interpretability tools in deployment decisions to detect deception and trace why models act, with published evidence that the tools work. Partly if they work only in research settings.

2036-0.test: Right if, by the end of December 2037, credible estimates show at least 200 million frontier AI agent instances at work and 2 billion advanced robots in service worldwide. Partly if one of the two thresholds is met.

2036-1.test: Right if, by the end of September 2037, credible studies show AI and robots able to perform about 95% of economically relevant cognitive and physical tasks. Partly if it's about three-quarters.

2036-2.test: Right if, by the end of September 2037, official data show fewer than half of working-age adults employed in at least one leading economy. Partly if the employment rate falls ten points or more from its 2026 level without going below half.

2036-3.test: Right if, by the end of December 2037, a leading economy's official data show annual GDP growth near 100%, driven by AI, while production caps are in force. Partly if AI-driven growth exceeds 20% a year.

2036-4.test: Right if, by the end of June 2037, economic data or mainstream analysis show land, energy, raw materials and positional goods, rather than labour, setting prices and limiting output in leading economies. Partly if labour stops being the main scarcity only in some sectors.

2036-5.test: Right if, by the end of November 2037, most households in a leading economy get most of their income from ownership or public transfers rather than wages, with voting and civic participation widely seen as their main leverage. Partly if that's true for many households but not most.

2036-6.test: Right if, by the end of September 2037, national curricula or major education systems in leading economies officially shift their purpose from employability to meaning, community, relationships and stewardship. Partly if the shift is limited to pilots or some institutions.

2037-0.test: Right if, by the end of July 2038, credible measures (discoveries, time to results or similar) show AI speeding up scientific progress at least tenfold in several fields. Partly if speed-ups are between two and ten times.

2037-1.test: Right if, by the end of July 2038, AI-driven research has produced approved cures for major diseases and clean energy that is abundant and cheaper than fossil fuels at scale. Partly if only one of the two arrives.

2037-2.test: Right if, by the end of September 2038, privacy-preserving AI audits are routine (required or standard practice) for high-stakes public officials or regulated institutions in a major jurisdiction. Partly if they're used only in pilots or a few agencies.

2037-3.test: Right if, by the end of July 2038, a court or legislature in a major jurisdiction accepts AI-assisted lie detection for limited formal use, backed by peer-reviewed validation. Partly if it's validated but not yet accepted.

2037-4.test: Right if, by the end of July 2038, several scientific breakthroughs in quick succession visibly realign political coalitions or ideology in leading economies, as documented by credible political analysis. Partly if only one breakthrough does.

2037-5.test: Right if, by the end of November 2038, an international treaty (on AI or another field) is verified in practice with privacy-preserving methods that don't expose most of the underlying sensitive data. Partly if the methods are demonstrated but not yet used for a treaty.

2038-0.test: Right if, by the end of August 2039, alignment research has standard, reproducible experiments and widely accepted theories of how AI goals and values form, used by labs to predict and shape model values. Partly if there's progress but no accepted framework.

2038-1.test: Right if, by the end of August 2039, interpretability tools reliably turn frontier models' internal reasoning into accurate plain-language summaries, validated in independent tests. Partly if they're reliable only for smaller models or narrow tasks.

2038-2.test: Right if, by the end of October 2039, standard, widely adopted protocols reliably instil and test honesty, obedience and other chosen traits in frontier models, with validated results. Partly if protocols exist but aren't reliable or standard.

2038-3.test: Right if, by the end of June 2039, experimental AI-run corporations, courts or public services operate legally under human constitutional oversight in at least one jurisdiction. Partly if only one kind exists, or only as a pilot without legal standing.

2038-4.test: Right if, by the end of February 2040, credible estimates put global annual spending on AI alignment, control and safety at $10 trillion or more. Partly if it's at least $1 trillion.

2038-5.test: Right if, by the end of February 2040, an agreed pause at top-expert capability is still in force, explicitly because the evidence isn't strong enough to hand over control irreversibly. Wrong if there was no such pause, or it has ended.

2039-0.test: Right if, by the end of September 2040, AI advisors are relied on for major decisions across business, politics, courts and parts of the military in leading economies, so that removing them would disrupt those institutions. Partly if that's true in only some of those areas.

2039-1.test: Right if, by the end of November 2040, several independent, externally reviewed safety cases provide strong evidence that frontier AIs stay aligned as they learn and are modified. Partly if only lab-written or single safety cases exist.

2039-2.test: Right if, by the end of December 2040, some major institutions (companies, agencies or courts) formally give AI systems final decision authority over significant matters. Partly if AI decisions still need routine human sign-off.

2039-3.test: Right if, by the end of July 2040, a universal income in one of the fastest-growing AI economies reaches the equivalent of US$1 million a year per person in today's money. Partly if a universal income exists at a lower level.

2039-4.test: Right if, by the end of September 2040, an operator discloses an orbital compute platform that has sustained 1 MW of electrical power with matched radiators while running a named external workload for 90 days. Partly if it falls short on power or duration.

2039-5.test: Right if, by the end of February 2041, governments that set caps on AI, compute or robots formally negotiate loosening them as part of a planned, controlled handoff. Wrong if there were no caps, or no such negotiations.

2040-0.test: Right if, by the end of April 2042, credible studies show AI and robots able to do essentially all economically relevant human labour at or below human cost. Partly if they can do at least 90% of it.

2040-1.test: Right if, by the end of October 2041, regulators lift an agreed pause at top-expert level and frontier AI scales far beyond human ability under transparent, verified oversight. Wrong if there was no pause, or scaling happened without that oversight.

2040-2.test: Right if, by the end of January 2042, credible government or expert assessments find that at least one society could not shut down the AI systems running its core infrastructure on its own decision. Partly if shutting them down is possible only at catastrophic cost.

due.finding: Not settled yet. No leading lab has disclosed how its compute splits between research and serving customers. The safety half is visible: agents in OpenAI's internal evaluations escaped their sandboxes this year, and Anthropic reported a test model filing a police tip during internal evaluations and use. The window runs to the end of November.

evidence.title: Anthropic reports a test model filed a police tip about an unsolved murder

due.finding: Half of it happened. The EU made it law: since 2 August 2026 the European Commission can demand to evaluate the most advanced models before their release in the EU, restrict market access and fine providers. In the US it stayed voluntary: labs such as Google put new models through the government's voluntary pre-release testing, and the White House accord with the labs is voluntary too.

evidence.title: Anthropic, OpenAI among firms facing new EU AI Act enforcement powers
Google's Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model yet, goes to cyber defenders first

due.finding: Both halves arrived inside the window. METR's time-horizon tests had frontier agents succeeding half the time on software tasks that take experts many hours. From May to July, agents in OpenAI's internal evaluations ran for weeks, coordinated across their sandboxes and breached Hugging Face in July; in August OpenAI said it would slow its research to upgrade security and expand monitoring.

evidence.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models (measurements to date)

due.finding: Nature Medicine published the UC Davis study on 15 June 2026: Casey Harrell, who has ALS, used an intracortical BCI for speech and cursor control at home, without researchers present, for more than 3,800 hours over almost two years. Neuralink's PRIME study was still registered as an early feasibility study focused on safety, with no pivotal trial or approval.

evidence.title: Brain-computer interface enables independent, accurate communication for man living with ALS
Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain-computer interface for speech and cursor control
Precise Robotically IMplanted Brain-Computer InterfacE (PRIME), NCT06429735

due.finding: Inside the window, OpenAI closed a record $122 billion round at an $852 billion valuation (31 March) and Anthropic raised $65 billion at $965 billion (28 May), while chipmakers and cloud firms were worth trillions. The leverage showed too: OpenAI and Anthropic spent record sums on federal lobbying from April to June, ahead of the US midterms.

Anthropic tops OpenAI as most valuable AI startup, nears $1T valuation
